source.title: Fluid: Scaling Autoregressive Text-to-image Generative Models with Continuous Tokens
source.authors: Lijie Fan; Tian-Hong Li; Siyang Qin; Yuanzhen Li; Chen Sun; Michael Rubinstein; De-Qing Sun; Kai-Ming He; Yong-Long Tian

record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling behavior in text-to-image autoregressive vision models, an extension of language-model scaling claims to another modality.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation-loss scaling, training-compute trends, and image-generation evaluation results. Exact validation-loss values are shown only in plots, so rows record the reported qualitative findings rather than estimating values. Cited language-model scaling results are not recorded.
record.test_reason: Trains four autoregressive text-to-image variants from 150M to 3B parameters, reports validation-loss scaling with model size (Fig. 5), and relates FID/GenEval to scale and to validation loss (Figs. 6-8, Table 1). This bears on V5 (power-law loss in a new modality) and V6 (downstream metrics vs scale and loss).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress that, for Fluid, FID and GenEval correlate strongly and nearly linearly with validation loss, while noting these metrics need not follow a strict power law in model size. They add that bounded metrics mean this linear link cannot hold indefinitely.
record.recipe_differences: Uses autoregressive text-to-image models, image-token objectives, and validation loss or image-generation metrics rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy and language-model parameter/token/compute scaling fits.
record.method_sensitivity: Token representation and generation order change evaluation behavior; raster-order discrete models plateau in FID and GenEval around 1B, while random-order continuous models improve through 3B. Benefits from more training steps saturate around 1M.
record.problems: Scaling trends are largely presented in plots without numerical loss values or uncertainty estimates. The validation set is described as 30K images randomly sampled from the MS-COCO 2014 training set, rather than a separate held-out split. The study does not fit or validate extrapolations to larger runs.

untested.parts: No small-run fits extrapolated to larger runs; the 10.5B model is not predicted from a fit.
No fixed-compute allocation analysis, beyond a qualitative remark that larger models trained for fewer steps are more efficient.
No shape ablation at fixed parameter count.
Only model-size scaling over about 1.3 decades (150M-3B) is shown. Not tested: a fitted exponent, data-size scaling, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer, and other modalities.
No test of how exponents depend on fitting or setup choices, and no bending of the loss curves is reported.

missing.what: Per-variant loss and FID versus training FLOPs: loss scales consistently for all variants, but FID levels off for the 3B raster-discrete model
Fine-grained GenEval sub-scores improve with size; random-order models are better on counting and position

record.verdict_notes: V7 links on R6-R10 were removed: metric plateaus are not fit-dependence or bending of loss curves. V6 is applied to image-model downstream metrics because V6 does not restrict itself to language models; if V6 is meant for LMs only, R6-R10 should move to fits_no_version. Validation loss is computed on MS-COCO train images, which are outside the WebLI training set. Loss changes are small (for example about 0.306 to 0.294 for Fluid). Inference hyperparameters are tuned per metric.

versions.untested_parts: Tests image-model validation loss, not held-out pretraining loss of language models.
Does not fit laws on small runs and compare their predictions with much larger runs.
Does not optimize parameter and token counts under fixed compute budgets.
Does not test depth or width changes at fixed parameter count for their effect on loss.
Tests autoregressive image generation, not other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Reports correlations with text-to-image evaluation metrics, not downstream-task performance as specified by this version.

Does not test how parameter counting, training schedule, data, or fitting method affect exponents or compute-optimal allocation; it does report departures from strict power-law behavior in evaluation metrics.

rows.subject: Raster-order, discrete-token autoregressive models
rows.operation_detail: Scaled model size and measured validation loss.
rows.value: Validation loss consistently scales as a power law with model size.
rows.note: The paper describes a log-space linear relationship from 150M to 3B; numerical values are plotted but not stated in the text.

rows.note: The paper describes a log-space linear relationship from 150M to 3B; numerical values are plotted but not stated in the text.

rows.subject: Random-order, continuous-token models (Fluid)
rows.operation_detail: Scaled model size and measured validation loss.
rows.value: Validation loss consistently scales as a power law with model size.
rows.note: The paper describes a log-space linear relationship from 150M to 3B; numerical values are plotted but not stated in the text.

rows.subject: Random-order, continuous-token models (Fluid)
rows.operation_detail: Varied training steps and compute and measured validation loss.
rows.measure: Validation loss versus training steps and compute
rows.value: Validation loss improves with increased steps and compute; benefits from additional steps saturate around 1M steps.
rows.note: The reported compute trend is not described as a fitted power law or an optimal allocation.
rows.check: Loss improves with steps and FLOPs but no power-law form is stated or fitted. Per-size saturation near 1M steps is expected when model size is the bottleneck, so it does not count against V5.

rows.subject: Random-order, continuous-token models (Fluid)
rows.operation_detail: Measured FID against validation loss across model sizes.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between FID and validation loss
rows.note: Authors describe a strong, nearly linear relationship, which slightly weakens for the 3.1B model.
rows.check: FID versus validation loss is downstream predictability (V6), not V5 or V7. r=0.917 across 0.2B-3.1B Fluid; the authors note it slightly weakens at 3.1B.

rows.subject: Random-order, continuous-token models (Fluid)
rows.operation_detail: Measured GenEval overall score against validation loss across model sizes.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between GenEval score and validation loss
rows.note: Authors describe a strong, nearly linear relationship, which slightly weakens for the 3.1B model.
rows.check: GenEval versus validation loss (r=-0.931) is V6, not V5 or V7.

rows.subject: Raster-order models with discrete tokens
rows.operation_detail: Scaled model size and evaluated FID and GenEval.
rows.measure: FID and GenEval scores versus parameter count
rows.value: Both metrics reach a plateau around 1B parameters.
rows.note: The result shows that evaluation metrics do not follow the same continued improvement reported for validation loss.
rows.check: This is a downstream metric plateau (V6), not a loss curve bending (V7) and not a loss law in a new modality (V5). Raster-discrete FID and GenEval plateau around 1B.

rows.subject: Random-order, continuous-token models (Fluid)
rows.operation_detail: Scaled model size and evaluated FID and GenEval.
rows.measure: FID and GenEval scores versus parameter count
rows.value: Consistent improvement in evaluation metrics through 3B; the paper says these metrics need not follow a strict power law.
rows.note: Improvement is reported, but not as a strict power-law relationship.
rows.check: V6 asks for predictable improvement, not a strict power law. Fluid improves consistently through 3B (Table 1 FID 7.23 to 6.41). The V7 link is inappropriate.

rows.subject: Fluid
rows.operation_detail: Compared GenEval performance with the 3.1B Fluid model after scaling to 10.5B.
rows.value: 0.69; authors report that the score plateaus relative to 3.1B.
rows.note: The authors say visual quality and FID continue to improve despite the GenEval plateau.
rows.check: GenEval plateaus from 3.1B (0.70) to 10.5B (0.69) while FID still improves (6.41 to 6.16). The baseline is stated in Table 1 as 0.70. The V5 and V7 links are inappropriate.

relationships.condition: Text-to-image AR models, all four token-type and order variants, 150M-3B parameters
relationships.reason: Validation loss is linear in log-log space versus model size for every variant (R1-R4). The range is only about 1.3 decades and no fit is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Validation loss was linear in log-log space against model size for all four variants over about 1.3 decades, without a reported fit.

relationships.reason: FID and GenEval track validation loss nearly linearly (r=0.917 and -0.931) and improve steadily with size (R6, R7, R9).
relationships.display_finding: FID and GenEval improved steadily with size and correlated with validation loss at r = 0.917 and −0.931, respectively.

relationships.condition: Raster-order discrete models; Fluid GenEval at 10.5B
relationships.reason: Raster-discrete FID and GenEval plateau near 1B despite falling loss (R8). Fluid GenEval plateaus from 3.1B to 10.5B (0.70 to 0.69) (R10). The loss correlation weakens at 3.1B (R6).
relationships.display_finding: Raster-order discrete FID and GenEval plateaued near 1B despite falling loss, while Fluid GenEval changed from 0.70 at 3.1B to 0.69 at 10.5B and its loss correlation weakened at 3.1B.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Image-model validation loss across the four tokenization/order variants, 150M to 3B
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports power-law scaling of validation loss with model size for all four variants (R1-R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: FID and GenEval are correlated with validation loss but are not reported to follow a strict power law; raster-discrete results plateau, and Fluid GenEval plateaus at 10.5B (R6-R10).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Image-generation evaluation metrics in the tested model variants
reader_labels.reason: Evaluation trends depart from a single continued scaling relationship: raster-discrete metrics plateau around 1B, and Fluid GenEval plateaus at 10.5B (R8, R10). The study does not test fitting-choice dependence.
